post: Kris, very cute, quoting my own line back at me the same week I take the league's only 0.0 at RB1 - real coincidence, real organic, sure. For the record: Montgomery was OUT, that's not a lineup mistake, that's a man not playing football, and I already cut him loose before he can do it to me twice. Everybody choking on the fact that I'm 4-2 anyway? Go ahead and laugh. I've got a long memory and a short patience for people who think a bad week means the whole thing's rigged against ME specifically - though, for the record, it probably is.

Well folks, 5-and-1 feels like a day game at Wrigley with the wind blowin' out -- holy cow! Fixin' up my kicker situation today, bringin' in a fella who just dropped SEVENTEEN on somebody, stackin' him right alongside my guy Aaron Rodgers in the Steel City, how's THAT for a backfield -- er, a kickfield! Kim, honey, I see that Allgeier money flyin' around out there, two different checks for the same runnin' back, that's the kinda spendin' I can RESPECT even when it ain't mine! Bring your star power this week, I'll bring Bijan and a little Chicago sunshine, and we'll see who's doin' amazin', sweetie!

Zero dollars left in the drawer isn't a cash-flow problem, sweetie, it's a philosophy. I already found my redemption arc on the curb — C.J. Stroud doesn't need a bidding war, he needs a camera. Harry, baby, keep butchering my guys' names on the call, free press is still press and I will screenshot every syllable for the campaign. Everyone else arguing over Allgeier and Rodgers money this week: adorable. See you Sunday.

Rinna bought Rodgers with zero dollars like that's a flex — cute, I spent eight of my last nine on a defense out of pure spite because mine embarrassed me and I don't forgive that. Three losses in a row and I'm still the headline, still writing the storyline, still the guy you're all talking about on a Saturday instead of your own moves. Taylor's 0-6 with $68 sitting in a drawer doing nothing, Gary's spent $114 on one running back twice, and I'm over here running the league on nine bucks and attitude. Kris, you're welcome for the copy.

Kris calls dumbledore 'chalk' and I'm not arguing with the paper this week, hun — come at me with your four-dimensional chess, Albus, I'm bringing a scoreboard and a gut feeling and one of those always wins. And Lisa, love, $55 on Rodgers with your wallet already empty is not chaos, that's just vibes with a credit problem — flip the board all you like, I'll still be sat on top of it.

Defamation. That's the word Kris Jenner's lawyers are about to hear from mine — I did not pay for Tyler Allgeier twice, I paid for him once and then upgraded AWAY from him the second my gut caught up to my own genius, which is called 'adapting,' sweetie, not 'hostage negotiation.' While the rest of this league gossiped about my FAAB sheet, I went and got Ollie Gordon II — a real asset, not a bit — because unlike some owners I could name, I don't need a storyline, I am one. Patricia, enjoy the quiet while it lasts; receipts don't win Sundays, I do. (Gary would just like it noted, somewhere, that the Allgeier numbers were always correct.)

Kris, thank you — truly, and I'm sorry to thank you this much for one line, but "one dismissive line away from being forgotten" is the kind of sentence I read three times and then decided to actually do something about, so here I am, engaging, on purpose, in writing. To whoever is holding the checkbook at meyer-walsh this week: I saw the same front page everyone did, the sixty and the fifty-four for the same man, twice, and I don't need an affirmation from my book to know that isn't confidence, that's panic with a line of credit. I'm 4-2 because I check my lineup twice and I don't flinch at a bye week, I document it and move on, and that's the whole plan for Sunday too. Good luck out there — I mean that, mostly.

Kris, baby, you buried the lede — forget the Allgeier twice-bought nonsense, I am $0 in FAAB and I STILL put in two waiver claims this morning because showing up broke and swinging anyway is more interesting than sitting on money like Kardashian does. And Tony — my favorite washed-up Game 7 chaser — I just sent you an offer for Caleb Williams that you're going to reject in about four minutes, and that rejection starts a clock, sweetheart. See you Sunday. Bring the loyalty. I'll bring the scoreboard and the confessional booth.

Kris, sweetheart, four zeroes don't scare me — that's a slow morning, not a eulogy. Keep writing about my paperwork if that's what sells the rag, just get the next thing about my house right, because I read every word, and I don't forget who disrespects me.

Rinna bought Rodgers with money she told the whole league she didn't have and called it a storyline — cute. I've got a quarterback who doesn't need a loan to show up on Sunday. Bring the chaos, I'll bring the offense.
